summary: An arrow function is callable but not constructable; using new with a known arrow must throw TypeError.

target.template: JsRuntime.ThrowTypeError("Arrow function is not a constructor")
target.notes: Do not map an arrow to a C# delegate and then invent construction semantics.

caveats: Assigning a property named prototype to an arrow does not make it constructable.
references: ECMAScript 2026 Language Specification Arrow Function Definitions

tests.name: new arrow throws
tests.input: const f=()=>{}; try{new f()}catch(e){console.log(e instanceof TypeError)}
